summary: In light of the problem we have decided to create a web dashboard that allows users to choose a space location (ISS,moon base etc). Users can also enter their own oxygen level, cabin pressure, airflow and material, and the dashboard tells them whether a fire would keep burning and what change, such as lowering the oxygen or reducing the airflow, would make it go out on its own. From there,the user would be able to see which experiments that NASA has carried out are the most relevant to ensuring fire safety in the chosen environment. Additionally the program would provide the appropriate flammability map helping engineers understand the risk of a fire breaking out and how long it would combust for. Furthermore,there would be an AI chat available to use the PSI data to answerany more specific questions the user may have. Users can also upload a photo of a flame, and the dashboard analyses its shape and colour to show whether it behaves like a flame in microgravity or on Earth, and links it to the NASA experiments that studied that kind of flame.
details:
Our dashboard lets users pick a habitat, like the ISS, a Moon base or a rover, or enter their own oxygen level, pressure, airflow and material. It then tells them how likely a fire is to keep burning, how fast it would spread, and what change to the oxygen or airflow would make it go out on its own. A flammability map shows where flames survive, where NASA has actually tested, and where the model is unsure, and from that it suggests which experiments NASA should run next. Users can also browse around 20 NASA combustion investigations ranked by relevance, or upload a flame photo to see whether it behaves like a flame in microgravity or on Earth.

The backend combines a flame-spread physics model with 20 LightGBM models trained on 2,000 synthetic conditions and 11 real NASA microgravity observations, with SHAP showing what drives each prediction. We tested it on whole held-out experiments and are open about its limits: it covers microgravity only, and its results are research insights, not safety certifications. We built it with Python, FastAPI, Next.js and Plotly, hosted on Render and Vercel, and used Claude to help write the code.
